title: CNF Encodings of Machine Configurations
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, with a finite state set, and let $n,s$ be natural numbers. There is a positive integer $C$, independent of $n,s$, such that for every $n,s$ one can choose an encoding of configurations and CNF formulas $\varphi_v,\varphi_a,\varphi_{\mathrm{acc}}$ with these properties: every configuration encoding has length $C(s+n+1)$; for inputs of length $n$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin, equal encodings imply equal inputs, and for a fixed input two configurations have equal encodings exactly when their states, input-head positions, work tapes, work-tape-head positions, and output summaries agree. The formula $\varphi_v$, evaluated on any bit string of that encoding length (with variables beyond the string assigned false), accepts exactly the encodings of such configurations on inputs of length $n$. The formula $\varphi_a$, evaluated on the concatenation of two configuration encodings, accepts exactly when the first configuration's one-step successor under $M$ has the same state, input-head position, work tapes, and work-tape-head positions as the second; it rejects every such pair whose inputs differ. The formula $\varphi_{\mathrm{acc}}$ accepts a configuration encoding exactly when the configuration is halted and its output is precisely the one-bit string $1$. The variable counts of $\varphi_v$ and $\varphi_{\mathrm{acc}}$ are at most $C(s+n+1)$, and that of $\varphi_a$ is at most $2C(s+n+1)$. Each of their binary CNF encodings has length at most $C(s+n+2)^C$.
